classification.difficultyReason: Converts the two horizontal boundaries into logarithmic x-coordinates and extends the taught rectangle-subtraction method to two nonzero heights, selecting the rectangles and exponential integral that isolate the requested area.

content.prompt: Find the area between the curve $y=2e^x$, the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=3$ and $y=5$.

spec.description: Equation-driven exponential graph with arrowheads, labelled axes and source ticks. The green region is bounded by the y-axis, the curve and both horizontal lines y=3 and y=5. Source red and green are represented by standard palette accents.
spec.mathematics: Curve y=2e^x passes through (0,2). The horizontal boundaries meet the curve at x=ln(3/2) and x=ln(5/2).
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied graphical givens appear; intersection x-values and the area are withheld.

answer.worked:
The horizontal boundaries meet the curve at
$$\begin{align*}
3&=2e^a,&a&=\ln\frac32,\\
5&=2e^b,&b&=\ln\frac52.
\end{align*}$$
Subtract the lower rectangle and the area under the curve from the upper rectangle.
$$\begin{align*}
A&=5b-3a-\int_a^b2e^x\,dx\\
A&=5b-3a-\left[2e^x\right]_a^b\\
A&=5\ln\frac52-3\ln\frac32-(5-3)\\
A&=\left(5\ln\frac52-3\ln\frac32-2\right)\text{ units}^2.
\end{align*}$$
